item.title: Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra: Whatever forms there be, In this world or the next, With excellent…
item.description:
Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra:

Whatever forms there be,
In this world or the next,
With excellent color,
Shining in the sky,
All those forms
Praised by Māra,
Are merely bait
Thrown out to catch fish.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.30

item.title: He again takes hold of internal contact and considers: 'But this craving, where does it arise, where does it settle?' He, taking hold of internal…
item.description:
He again takes hold of internal contact and considers: 'But this craving, where does it arise, where does it settle?' He, taking hold of internal contact, knows: 'Whatever in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles. And what in the world is agreeable and enticing? The eye in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles.' ... The ear in the world ... the nose in the world ... the tongue in the world ... the body in the world ... the mind in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.66

item.title: Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering.…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering. They delight in sound ... in odor ... in taste ... in touch ... Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in mind-objects, are excited by mind-objects. When mind-objects change, fade away, and cease, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering. Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having truly understood the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape regarding form, does not delight in form, does not enjoy form, is not excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata lives in happiness. He does not delight in sound ... in odor ... in taste ... in touch ... Having truly understood the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape regarding mind-objects, the Tathāgata does not delight in mind-objects, does not enjoy them, is not excited by them. When mind-objects change, fade away, and cease, the Tathāgata lives in happiness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.136

item.title: I declare to you, bhikkhus, I make known to you, bhikkhus: For an immoral person, of evil character, impure, it would be better to have…
item.description:
I declare to you, bhikkhus, I make known to you, bhikkhus: For an immoral person, of evil character, impure, it would be better to have a strong man take a red-hot iron plate, blazing, flaming, and wrap it around his body. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, from that cause he might meet death or death-like suffering, but not because of that cause, after death, with the breakup of the body, would he be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. But when an immoral person, of evil character, impure in conduct... impure, enjoys the robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites offered out of faith by wealthy nobles, wealthy brahmins, or wealthy householders, then, bhikkhus, that leads to his long-term harm and suffering, and after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.
Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: 'When we enjoy the requisites such as robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites of those donors, may our conduct be of great fruit and great benefit. And may our going forth not be in vain, but fruitful and rewarding.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.72

item.title: 'The removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the synonym for the removal of…
item.description:
'The removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the synonym for the removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion?" - "It is a synonym for the Nibbāna element, bhikkhu, and is also called the destruction of the taints." When this was said, that bhikkhu said: "'The Deathless, the Deathless,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the Deathless, Venerable Sir? What is the path leading to the Deathless?" - "The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion, bhikkhu, is called the Deathless. This Noble Eightfold Path is the path leading to the Deathless, that is, right view ... right concentration.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 45.7

item.title: Do not kill living beings, Do not take what is not given, Do not speak falsehood, Do not drink intoxicants; Abandon non-celibacy, Abandon, do not…
item.description:
Do not kill living beings,
Do not take what is not given,
Do not speak falsehood,
Do not drink intoxicants;
Abandon non-celibacy,
Abandon, do not commit sexual misconduct,
Do not eat at night,
Avoid eating at improper times.

Do not wear garlands,
Do not use perfumes,
Lie on a mat
Spread on the ground;
This eight-factored observance,
Called the uposatha,
Proclaimed by the Buddha,
Leads to the end of suffering.

The moon and sun,
Seen as beautiful,
Wherever they go,
They shine with radiance;
They make the clouds bright,
Traveling through the sky,
They shine in the heavens,
Illuminating all directions.

In that space,
Treasures are found,
Pearls and gems,
Beryl, lucky stones;
Gold nuggets in the earth,
Or the kind called Kancana,
And the bright gold
Called Hattaka.

Yet they are worth
Only one-sixteenth part
Of the observance of the uposatha,
Complete with all eight factors,
Including the moon's light,
Including the starry sky.

Therefore, women and men,
Let them keep pure precepts,
Practice the uposatha observance,
Complete with all eight factors;
Do meritorious deeds,
Bringing great happiness,
Reborn in heaven,
Not mocked by people.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.70

item.title: Cunda, this situation may occur: wanderers of other sects might say: 'Regarding the past, Samaṇa Gotama has supernormal knowledge. But regarding the future, Samaṇa Gotama…
item.description:
Cunda, this situation may occur: wanderers of other sects might say: 'Regarding the past, Samaṇa Gotama has supernormal knowledge. But regarding the future, Samaṇa Gotama has no supernormal knowledge; as to how things happen and why they happen thus?' Thus these wanderers, being foolish and unintelligent, hold that knowledge of one matter can be explained by knowledge of another. Cunda, regarding the past, the Tathāgata can recollect past lives. As he wishes, he can recollect that far back. Regarding the future, the Tathāgata has knowledge born of wisdom: 'This is the last birth, now there is no further existence.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 29 – Pāsādikasutta

item.title: Rāhula, when you wish to do a mental action, you should reflect on that same mental action: 'Does this mental action I wish to do…
item.description:
Rāhula, when you wish to do a mental action, you should reflect on that same mental action: 'Does this mental action I wish to do lead to my own harm, to others' harm, to the harm of both? Is this mental action unwholesome, leading to suffering, with painful results?' Rāhula, if, on reflection, you know: 'This mental action I wish to do leads to my own harm, to others' harm, to the harm of both; it is unwholesome, leading to suffering, with painful results' — then such a mental action you should definitely not do. Rāhula, if, on reflection, you know: 'This mental action I wish to do does not lead to my own harm, not to others' harm, not to the harm of both; it is wholesome, leading to happiness, with pleasant results' — then such a mental action you should do.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 61 – Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasutta

item.title: Fear and suffering, Illness and boil, Both clinging and swamp, Are called sensual pleasures. There the ordinary person, Infatuated and clinging, Sees fear in clinging,…
item.description:
Fear and suffering,
Illness and boil,
Both clinging and swamp,
Are called sensual pleasures.
There the ordinary person,
Infatuated and clinging,
Sees fear in clinging,
The origin of birth and death.
Without clinging, liberated,
Birth and death are destroyed,
They attain security,
Pure bliss in this life,
Overcome fear and enmity,
All suffering is overcome.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.23

item.title: - Friends, defilement is called defilement — what is the synonym for what is called defilement? - Friends, evil, unwholesome states, the domain of sensual…
item.description:
- Friends, defilement is called defilement — what is the synonym for what is called defilement?
- Friends, evil, unwholesome states, the domain of sensual desire, are the synonym for what is called defilement.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta
